etymology: Webster 1828 treats THEMSELVES as a compound of them and selves, added to they for emphasis or pointed distinction (they themselves have done the mischief); sometimes standing as the only nominative (themselves have done the mischief); and also in the objective after a verb or preposition (things in themselves innocent). This page fills the KJV-gap reflexive of the nations and the flesh. Companion pages already treat himself, man, and fool.
biblical_def: Themselves in Scripture is not a therapy word and not a brand of authenticity. It names what the nations must learn they are, what rebels set in array, and what the flesh gives itself to. The psalmist will not let empire keep its costume: that the nations may know themselves to be but men (Psa 9:20). The kings will not be allowed a third party: The kings of the earth set themselves, and the rulers take counsel together, against the LORD, and against his anointed (Psa 2:2). The apostle will not baptize self-praise: Professing themselves to be wise, they became fools (Rom 1:22). The old walk is not a lifestyle: have given themselves over unto lasciviousness, to work all uncleanness with greediness (Eph 4:19). Levi will not stay in the camp of the calf: all the sons of Levi gathered themselves together unto him (Exo 32:26). The dictionary therefore keeps themselves from becoming either a gospel of self or a crowd that outvotes the Anointed. It is the Bible’s way of saying: they, not God — and they will answer.
webster_summary: Webster 1828 defines THEMSELVES as a compound of them and selves, added to they for emphasis or pointed distinction; sometimes used as the only nominative; and also in the objective after a verb or preposition.
webster_full: THEMSELVES', a compound of them and selves, and added to they by way of emphasis or pointed distinction. Thus we say, they themselves have done the mischief; they cannot blame others. In this case, themselves is in the nominative case, and maybe considered as an emphatical pronoun.
In some cases, themselves is used without they, and stands as the only nominative to the following verb. themselves have done the mischief.
This word is used also in the objective case after a verb or preposition. Things in themselves innocent, may under certain circumstances cease to be so.
They open to themselves at length the way.
scriptures: Psalm 9:20
Put them in fear, O LORD: that the nations may know themselves to be but men. Selah.
Psalm 2:2
The kings of the earth set themselves, and the rulers take counsel together, against the LORD, and against his anointed, saying,
Romans 1:22
Professing themselves to be wise, they became fools,
Ephesians 4:19
Who being past feeling have given themselves over unto lasciviousness, to work all uncleanness with greediness.
Exodus 32:26
Then Moses stood in the gate of the camp, and said, Who is on the LORD'S side? let him come unto me. And all the sons of Levi gathered themselves together unto him.
corruption_summary: Themselves is corrupted when authenticity is treated as righteousness, when self-profession is baptized as wisdom, and when giving themselves over to lust is sold as liberation.
corruption_paragraphs: The first corruption is authenticity-as-gospel. Psalm 9:20 is the nations knowing themselves to be but men. Therapeutic religion keeps the pronoun and drops the fear of the LORD. Be yourselves is not the sermon. The recovery is that they are men, not gods.

The second corruption is Romans 1:22 as a compliment. Professing themselves to be wise, they became fools is indictment. Credential culture and expressive-self talk treat self-narration as light. The dictionary will not. The mouth that certifies itself is already dark.

The third corruption is Ephesians 4:19 as freedom. They have given themselves over unto lasciviousness. The age calls that honesty. Scripture calls it greed for uncleanness. Levi in Exodus 32:26 gathered themselves together unto Moses, not unto the calf. The reflexive is not a permission slip.
roots_summary: Webster: them + selves, emphatic / objective. roots_lines: Greek phasko (G5335) — to allege, to profess (Rom 1:22, Professing themselves).
Psalm 9:20 tags men (H582), not the English reflexive; Psalm 2:2 tags set (H3320), not themselves.
Exodus 32:26 is KJV-verified; the cache does not tag themselves with a Hebrew number on that verse line. No lemma is invented here.
usage: The nations must know themselves to be but men (Psa 9:20).
Kings set themselves against the LORD and His Anointed (Psa 2:2); fools profess themselves wise (Rom 1:22).
The old walk gives themselves over to lasciviousness (Eph 4:19); Levi gathered themselves unto Moses (Exo 32:26).

etymology: Webster 1828 treats OLD as adjective: advanced far in years; long made or used / decayed by time; of long continuance; not new or fresh; of a former year’s growth; ancient; of any duration (how old art thou?); subsisting before something else (the old law repealed by the new); long practiced; long cultivated; and, of old, long ago. His biblical illustration is Genesis 12:4, Abraham seventy-five years old. This page fills the KJV-gap adjective of age and the old man. Companion pages already treat age, child, and man.
biblical_def: Old in Scripture is not a brand and not a slur. It names the years the Lord carries, the child who will not depart, and the man in Adam who must be put off. The psalmist will not let gray hair write abandonment: I have been young, and now am old; yet have I not seen the righteous forsaken (Psa 37:25). The proverb will not let training be a mood: Train up a child in the way he should go: and when he is old, he will not depart from it (Pro 22:6). The apostle will not let the former conversation keep the pulpit: put off concerning the former conversation the old man, which is corrupt according to the deceitful lusts (Eph 4:22). Colossians will not let the deeds stay: ye have put off the old man with his deeds (Col 3:9). Isaiah will not let hoar hairs be a threat: even to your old age I am he; and even to hoar hairs will I carry you (Isa 46:4). The dictionary therefore keeps old from becoming either a youth-cult insult or a costume for the Adamic self. It is the Bible’s way of saying: years under God — and a man who must die.
webster_summary: Webster 1828 defines OLD as advanced in years; long used or decayed by time; of long continuance; not new; ancient; of any duration; prior to something else; long practiced; and of old, from ancient times. He illustrates from Genesis 12:4.
webster_full: OLD, adjective

1. Advanced far in years or life; having lived beyond the middle period, or rather towards the end of life, or towards the end of the ordinary term of living; applied to animals or plants; as an old man; an old age; an old camel or horse; an old tree.
Abraham was seventy five years old when he departed from Haran. Genesis 12:4.
2. Having been long made or used; decayed by time; as an old garment; an old house.
3. Being of long continuance; begun long ago; as an old acquaintance.
4. Having been long made; not new or fresh; as old wine.
6. Ancient; that existed in former ages; as the old inhabitants of Britain; the old Romans.
7. Of any duration whatever; as a year old; seven years old. How old art thou?
8. Subsisting before something else. He built a new house on the site of the old one. The old law is repealed by the new.
Of old, long ago; from ancient times; as in days of old.
scriptures: Psalm 37:25
I have been young, and now am old; yet have I not seen the righteous forsaken, nor his seed begging bread.
Proverbs 22:6
Train up a child in the way he should go: and when he is old, he will not depart from it.
Ephesians 4:22
That ye put off concerning the former conversation the old man, which is corrupt according to the deceitful lusts;
Colossians 3:9
Lie not one to another, seeing that ye have put off the old man with his deeds;
Isaiah 46:4
And even to your old age I am he; and even to hoar hairs will I carry you: I have made, and I will bear; even I will carry, and will deliver you.
corruption_summary: Old is corrupted when years are treated as disposable, when the old man is recast as a personality type, and when hoar hairs are emptied of the God who carries.
corruption_paragraphs: The first corruption is the youth-cult. Psalm 37:25 is a man now old who has not seen the righteous forsaken. The age discards gray hair and calls it progress. Isaiah 46:4 remains: even to your old age I am he. Years are not a defect in the people God carries.

The second corruption is Ephesians 4:22 as branding. The old man is corrupt according to deceitful lusts, put off with his deeds (Col 3:9). Therapeutic talk keeps old as a vibe — old-fashioned, old energy — and drops Adam. The dictionary will not. The old man is a nature, not a playlist.

The third corruption is Proverbs 22:6 as a slogan without a way. When he is old, he will not depart from it assumes a child trained in the way he should go. Sentiment keeps the proverb and loses the catechism. Age without the way is just more time in the old man.
roots_summary: Webster: advanced in years / long used / ancient. Verse-cache Strong’s on the quotations below: Hebrew zaqen (H2204) at Psalm 37:25 and Proverbs 22:6; Hebrew ziqnah (H2209) at Isaiah 46:4; Greek palaios (G3820) at Ephesians 4:22 and Colossians 3:9. Genesis 12:4 is Webster’s illustration; this page does not mint a number for that line beyond what the cache tags on the quotations used.
roots_lines: Hebrew zaqen (H2204) — to be old (Psa 37:25; Pro 22:6, when he is old).
Greek palaios (G3820) — old, worn, former (Eph 4:22; Col 3:9, the old man).
No extra lemma is invented for English old where the cache does not tag it.
usage: The psalmist has been young and is now old, and the righteous are not forsaken (Psa 37:25).
A child trained in the way will not depart when he is old (Pro 22:6).
Put off the old man with his deeds (Eph 4:22; Col 3:9); to old age the LORD carries His people (Isa 46:4).

etymology: Webster 1828 treats UNTIL as preposition from un and till: to, used of time (Judges 18:30, until the day of the captivity); to, used of objects (obsolete); preceding a clause, to the event or the time of it (Genesis 49:10, until Shiloh come); to the point or place of; to the degree that (2 Chronicles 18:10). He notes that the sense is in all cases to, and that till may stand as its substitute. This page fills the KJV-gap preposition of appointed time. Companion pages already treat time, end, and throne.
biblical_def: Until in Scripture is not a stall and not a mood. It names the appointed limit of waiting, of blindness, of tutors, and of the sceptre. David will not let the session be intern: Sit thou at my right hand, until I make thine enemies thy footstool (Psa 110:1). Paul will not let conceit write Israel off: blindness in part is happened to Israel, until the fulness of the Gentiles be come in (Rom 11:25). The heir will not stay a child: is under tutors and governors until the time appointed of the father (Gal 4:2). Jacob will not let Judah keep the stick forever as if Shiloh never comes: The sceptre shall not depart from Judah … until Shiloh come (Gen 49:10). The church will not invent a calendar to replace prayer: so our eyes wait upon the LORD our God, until that he have mercy upon us (Psa 123:2). The dictionary therefore keeps until from becoming either delay-as-denial or a human deadline. It is the Bible’s way of saying: to this event, at the Father’s time.
webster_summary: Webster 1828 defines UNTIL as to, used of time, event, place, or degree. The sense is always to; till may be used as its substitute. He illustrates from Judges 18:30, Genesis 49:10, and 2 Chronicles 18:10.
webster_full: UNTIL', preposition [un and till. See Till.]
1. To; used of time.
He and his sons were priests of the tribe of Dan, until the day of the captivity. Judges 18:30.
2. To; used of objects. obsolete.
3. Preceding a sentence or clause, to; that is, to the event mentioned, or the time of it; as, until this hour; until this year.
The scepter shall not depart from Judah - until Shiloh come. Genesis 49:10.
4. To the point or place of.
5. To the degree that.
Thou shalt push Syria, until they be consumed. 2 Chronicles 18:10.

Note. until is always the same part of speech in fact, and has the same signification. The only difference is that it is followed sometimes by a single word denoting time, and in other cases by a verb denoting an event, or a word denoting place or degree. The sense is in all cases to; and till may be used as its substitute.
scriptures: Psalm 110:1
The LORD said unto my Lord, Sit thou at my right hand, until I make thine enemies thy footstool.
Romans 11:25

For I would not, brethren, that ye should be ignorant of this mystery, lest ye should be wise in your own conceits; that blindness in part is happened to Israel, until the fulness of the Gentiles be come in.
Galatians 4:2
But is under tutors and governors until the time appointed of the father.
Genesis 49:10
The sceptre shall not depart from Judah, nor a lawgiver from between his feet, until Shiloh come; and unto him shall the gathering of the people be.
Psalm 123:2

Behold, as the eyes of servants look unto the hand of their masters, and as the eyes of a maiden unto the hand of her mistress; so our eyes wait upon the LORD our God, until that he have mercy upon us.
corruption_summary: Until is corrupted when the appointed time is treated as never, when Israel is written off before the fulness, and when waiting is replaced by a self-made deadline.
corruption_paragraphs: The first corruption is delay-as-denial. Psalm 110:1 is until I make thine enemies thy footstool. Process-God talk keeps the preposition and drops the session. The Son sits. The end is not a maybe. Galatians 4:2 remains the Father’s time appointed, not an open workshop.

The second corruption is Romans 11:25 inverted. Blindness in part is until the fulness of the Gentiles be come in. Conceit baptizes replacement as mercy and calls Israel finished. The mystery is not a license to erase the people. Genesis 49:10 still runs to Shiloh, not to a committee.

The third corruption is the self-deadline. Psalm 123:2 is eyes that wait until that he have mercy. The age sets timers, then calls God late. Mercy is not late. Until belongs to the LORD’s hand, not to ours.
roots_summary: Webster: to (time / event / degree). Verse-cache Strong’s on the quotations below: Greek achri (G891) at Romans 11:25 and Galatians 4:2. Psalm 110:1, Genesis 49:10, and Psalm 123:2 carry no Strong’s tag on until in this cache; this page does not mint one.
roots_lines: Greek achri (G891) — until, as far as (Rom 11:25; Gal 4:2).
Psalm 110:1 tags make (H7896) after English until, not the preposition itself.
Psalm 123:2 tags mercy (H2603) after English until, not the preposition itself.
Genesis 49:10 is KJV-verified as Webster’s illustration; the cache does not tag until with a Hebrew number on that verse line. No lemma is invented here.
usage: The Son sits at the right hand until His enemies are made a footstool (Psa 110:1).
Israel’s blindness in part is until the fulness of the Gentiles (Rom 11:25); the heir is under tutors until the Father’s appointed time (Gal 4:2).
The sceptre remains until Shiloh come (Gen 49:10); our eyes wait until He have mercy (Psa 123:2).
